title: Utility Types: Promises and Asynchronous Values knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a robust asynchronous API wrapper do?
options: Trust response.json() because its result is automatically verified by TypeScript.
Treat a declared response type as a server-side authorization check.
Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
questions.answer_key: Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
questions.explanation: The type checker does not validate remote data; asynchronous operations can fail independently.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Utility Types: Promises and Asynchronous Values”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with awaited and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with awaited and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Awaited”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Utility Types: Promises and Asynchronous Values”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check promise result types, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume composing asynchronous type transformations is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check promise result types, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Promise result types”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
